notes: Change (family F7, uncommitted): selectBuildInputs returns null when neither a vendor override nor the detected metadata has a dockerfilePath; the 'Dockerfile' default is removed. runLocalBuild then records build FAIL with detail 'production preflight blocks: dockerfile-missing' (evidence.failure 'preflight') and runs no docker build. Fixes repo-505, 515, 518, 525, 579, 585, 588, 590, 596.

Production rule read in packages/cdk/src/lambda/worker.ts buildRelease and packages/cdk/src/pipeline/build-pipeline.ts: dockerfilePath = override ?? detected ?? 'Dockerfile'; context = override ?? (detected dockerfileBuildContext only when no Dockerfile override) ?? top-level docker/ -> '.' ?? buildspec dirname($DOCKERFILE_PATH). The harness already copied this rule (a drift test guards it); no context change was needed. Production never reads manifest.build.context (the manifest default is '.').

Difference cause for repo-517, 536, 548, 577, 580: the first-run gate evidence shows the UNCONFIGURED analysis manifest (context '.', detected Dockerfile), but the build used the deploy-config vendor overrides (overrides.dockerfilePath), the same as production uses a stored PATCH override. 536 (docker/production/Dockerfile), 580 (docker/services/Dockerfile), 548 (.docker/Dockerfile) and 577 (docker/Dockerfile.server.multiarch.rootless) therefore built the override Dockerfile; with no buildContext override the production dir rule gave the Dockerfile directory (536 docker/production, 580 docker/services, 517 apiserver/src/main/docker, 548 .docker) while the manifest says '.'. 577 kept context '.' via the top-level docker/ rule. This is production behaviour, not a harness defect: 536 and 580 build when the deploy-config adds buildContext '.', which is a REPO_CONFIGURATION (deploy-config) change for the rerun, not a harness change. 517, 548, 577 fail for F1 causes (missing COPY sources or release tarball), as families.md says. A new test checks that an override Dockerfile uses the production dir rule.

Observation for the coordinator (product, not changed): the manifest build.context default '.' (manifest.ts) differs from the worker/buildspec dir rule for a nested Dockerfile with no context override; the gate and the build can disagree. Consider a product decision; out of scope here.
Only scripts/repository-deployment/ and docs/testing/compatibility.md changed; no docs/testing/*/runs/ file changed. Nothing committed. No Docker, AWS or network use.
